correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the two shapes with \(\Omega(n)=2\). Prime squares reduce exactly to \(S(r^2)=r\), and distinct-prime products reduce exactly to \(S(pq)\in\{p,q\}\). Modulo-9 congruences plus the monotone digit-length inequality leave only explicitly checked finite exceptions. The counting consequence then follows from uniform prime-counting bounds, Mertens prime-reciprocal growth, and Landau semiprime counting.

value.rationale: The Omega-two layer is the first nontrivial multiplicative layer, and the Moran definition itself is a factorization by the digit sum and a prime. Determining that the digit sum must equal the least prime factor is therefore an intrinsic structural classification. Its logarithmic least-factor bound yields an unconditional zero-density consequence among all semiprimes, so the result is more than a bounded census or routine restatement.
